info.name: Crehana Todo API (develop @ v1.0.0)
info.description:
FastAPI Todo Lists API - Crehana backend challenge (C:\Users\Alberto\Developer\personal\crehana-todo-api, branch develop, tag v1.0.0). Exercises auth, owner-scoped task lists/tasks, the status state machine, filtering + completion_percentage, assignment, and the error contract {code, message[, details]}.

Run order matters: folders 0-6 build and tear down one owner / one list / several tasks end to end. Folder 7 is optional and last.

Re-runnable: the collection-level pre-request script stamps a fresh `runId` (and derived emails/password) once per run, the first time it sees `runId` empty, so re-running the whole collection never collides with a previous run's data.

item.name: 0. Health
item.description: Liveness/readiness probes (src/app/infrastructure/api/routers/health.py). Mounted at the application root, NOT under /api/v1 -- every other endpoint in this collection is under /api/v1, health is the one exception.

request.description: Always 200 while the process is up, independent of the database (health.py:14-17). No auth required.
200 once the DB is reachable (SELECT 1), 503 otherwise (health.py:20-31). Requires `docker compose up --wait` to have passed the db healthcheck first.

item.name: 1. Auth
item.description: Registration, login, refresh and /users/me (auth.py, users.py). register/login/refresh/health use no auth; every later folder relies on the tokens captured here.

request.description: Creates the owner account used for the rest of the run (auth.py:33-51). Returns the public user shape {id, email, created_at} - never a password hash (schemas/users.py).
Registering the same email twice violates the unique-email rule -> 409 email_already_registered (domain/exceptions.py:62-66).

Password shorter than 8 chars fails the policy (8-128 chars, >=1 letter, >=1 digit - value_objects.py:82-92) -> 422 weak_password. Note: this error carries no `details` array, unlike schema-level validation errors - PasswordPolicyError takes no field argument (domain/exceptions.py:86-93).
Issues an access/refresh pair (auth.py:54-71, jwt.py:28-35: access TTL 15min, refresh TTL 7 days). Captures both tokens for every request later in the run.
Wrong password -> 401 invalid_credentials, the same error used for an unknown email entirely (no account-enumeration - auth/use_cases.py:58-78).
Exchanges the still-valid refresh token for a fresh pair (auth/use_cases.py:81-95). Overwrites the captured tokens so later requests use the freshest ones.
Authenticated identity lookup (users.py:22-33). Uses the collection-level Bearer {{accessToken}} - no auth override needed.
A missing Authorization header -> 401 not_authenticated (dependencies.py:97-98), distinct from an invalid/wrong-typed token.

item.name: Get /users/me with refresh token as bearer (401)

request.description: A refresh token carries `type: refresh` in its JWT claim; /users/me only accepts `type: access` -> 401 invalid_token even though the token itself is validly signed and unexpired (dependencies.py:85-99, security/jwt.py:37-50).
Registers the user who will later be assigned a task.
Captures the assignee's own access token for later requests.
Registers a third user with no relationship to the owner's list or tasks, used to prove the 404-not-403 no-enumeration rule (design ADR-06).
Captures the stranger's own access token.

item.name: 2. Task lists
item.description: Owner-scoped list CRUD (task_lists.py). Non-owner/nonexistent both -> 404, never 403 (design ADR-06).

request.description: Owner-scoped creation (task_lists.py:37-59). Saves `listId` for every later folder.
Per-owner name uniqueness is case-insensitive (task_lists/use_cases.py:22-33: `GROCERIES {{runId}}` collides with `Groceries {{runId}}`) -> 409 task_list_name_conflict.
An all-whitespace name passes the Pydantic schema (no min_length) but is rejected by the domain's blank-after-trim rule -> 422 invalid_field (value_objects.py:54-63).

exec: pm.test('contains the created list', () => pm.expect(body.some(l => l.id === pm.collectionVariables.get('listId'))).to.be.true);

request.description: Every list owned by the caller (task_lists.py:62-76).
Retrieve one owned list by id (task_lists.py:79-93).
Partial update - only `name` is sent, `description` stays untouched thanks to `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` (design ADR-04, task_lists.py:96-118).
A non-owner gets the exact same 404 as a nonexistent list - never 403 (design ADR-06, authorization.py:24-31).

item.name: 3. Tasks
item.description: Owner-scoped task CRUD and the strict 4-edge status state machine (tasks.py, value_objects.py:40-51). By the end of this folder: taskId is done, a high-priority task and a default-priority (medium) task also exist in the same list, for folder 4's filters.

request.description: Owner-scoped creation inside the list created above (tasks.py:52-80). Saves `taskId`; starts as status=pending.

exec: const yesterday = new Date(Date.UTC(now.getUTCFullYear(), now.getUTCMonth(), now.getUTCDate() - 1));

request.description: due_date is compared against the server's injected UTC clock (value_objects.py:95-103); a past date -> 422 due_date_in_past. Yesterday's UTC date is computed in a pre-request script so the test stays correct regardless of when it runs.
A second task, used by the priority filter in folder 4.
No `priority` sent -> defaults to medium (schemas/tasks.py:22-30: `priority: Priority = Priority.MEDIUM`, a slice-filled gap recorded in DECISION_LOG.md, not the spec itself).
Retrieve one owned task (tasks.py:122-137).
Partial update of description only (tasks.py:140-162).
The only edge out of pending (value_objects.py:40-46, 49-51).
A valid in_progress -> done edge.
Same-status transitions are rejected too, not just invalid ones - done's only outgoing edge is in_progress (value_objects.py:40-51).
done cannot skip straight back to pending; its only valid edge is -> in_progress (value_objects.py:42-46).
The only valid edge out of done.
Back to done, so folder 4's status=done filter has exactly one match.

item.name: 4. Filters & completion
item.description: Filtered/paginated listing and the list-wide completion_percentage (tasks.py:83-120, design ADR-10).

request.description: Of the 3 tasks in the list only `taskId` is done -> total=1. completion_percentage is computed over ALL tasks regardless of the filter (design ADR-10, tasks/use_cases.py:136-158): 1 done / 3 total = 33.33%.
Only the 'Buy eggs' task matches.
No filter: total still reflects all 3 tasks, but only 1 item is returned for this page (limit/offset never affect `total`).
`status` is a query-level enum (tasks.py:96); a value outside {pending, in_progress, done} fails FastAPI/Pydantic request validation -> 422 validation_error (errors.py:63-82), not a domain error.
`limit` has `ge=1` (tasks.py:98); 0 fails validation -> 422.

item.name: 5. Assignment
item.description: Owner-only assign/unassign and the assignee's own cross-list visibility (assignment/use_cases.py, task-assignment spec).

request.description: A well-formed but nonexistent user id -> 422 assignee_not_found (assignment/use_cases.py:44-47), not 404 - the assignee is a request field being validated, not the resource being addressed.

Owner-only assignment (assignment/use_cases.py:17-68). Triggers one fake email invitation AFTER the commit (design ADR-12) - look for it with `docker compose logs api | grep notifications`; it is not observable over HTTP so it is not asserted here.

exec: pm.test('contains the assigned task', () => pm.expect(body.items.some(t => t.id === pm.collectionVariables.get('taskId'))).to.be.true);

request.description: Cross-list visibility for the assignee, without owning the list (users.py:36-57, task-assignment spec).
The one status-change privilege a non-owner has (authorization.py:45-64, design ADR-06). taskId is currently `done` (end of folder 3), so `in_progress` is the only legal target here.

SURPRISE: GET is owner-only (`owned_task`), which checks list ownership first - so the assignee (who owns neither the list nor is checked here) gets 404 task_list_not_found, NOT task_not_found, even though the task itself exists and is assigned to them (authorization.py:33-43).
Same owner-only `owned_task` path as GET -> 404 task_list_not_found for the assignee too (tasks.py:165-179).

exec: pm.test('code is task_not_found (no list enumeration here)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().code).to.equal('task_not_found'));

request.description: SURPRISE: unlike GET/DELETE, the status endpoint uses `status_changeable_task`, which deliberately never reveals list existence first (authorization.py:45-64) -> 404 task_not_found here, a DIFFERENT code than the task_list_not_found the assignee got above for the exact same task, from a stranger who is neither owner nor assignee.
Explicit `null` clears the assignee (schemas/tasks.py:53-59: `assignee_id` is required here, unlike the generic PATCH's UNSET-aware fields). Unassigning never sends a notification (design ADR-12).
Owner deletes taskId (tasks.py:165-179).
Deletes the list, cascading its remaining tasks at the DB level (task_lists.py:121-133, task-lists spec).
The list is gone -> 404 task_list_not_found, same as it never having existed.

item.name: 7. Security (optional, last)
item.description: Security response headers and a rate-limit demonstration (security-hardening spec). The rate-limit request is manual by design - see its description.

request.description: security_headers_middleware (middleware.py:28-38) attaches these to every response, verified here on the cheapest endpoint.

item.name: Rate limit demonstration (manual - run several times fast)

request.description: AUTH_RATE_LIMIT=10/minute is enabled in docker-compose.yml (rate_limit.py). A single call from this collection run will almost always just be 401 (wrong password) - genuinely tripping 429 needs several rapid requests to the SAME auth route within 60s (slowapi scopes the limit per decorated route, not globally across register/login/refresh). Click Send repeatedly by hand (or use the Runner with a short delay) to see 429 with code rate_limited. The assertion below deliberately accepts either outcome so the automated run never depends on timing.
